## Summary

CodeQL open alert on default branch: **HIGH** `js/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization` — Incomplete URL substring sanitization.

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Alert | [#137](https://github.com/deftai/directive/security/code-scanning/137) |
| Rule | `js/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization` |
| Severity | HIGH |
| Location | `packages/core/src/intake/github-auth-modes.provisioning.test.ts` ~L174 |
| Message | 'ghe.example.com' can be anywhere in the URL, and arbitrary hosts may come before or after it. |

## What to build

Rewrite or bound the flagged site so CodeQL `js/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization` clears for this alert (or document accepted risk with suppress + rationale if false positive after review). Prefer a real fix over suite-config changes.

## Acceptance

- [ ] CodeQL alert [#137](https://github.com/deftai/directive/security/code-scanning/137) clears on master (auto-close or dismiss with reason after fix).
- [ ] Existing unit tests for the touched module still pass; add adversarial input coverage if useful.
- [ ] CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Security/Fixed entry citing CodeQL alert #137.

## Non-goals

- Changing CodeQL suite config as the primary fix.
- Bundling unrelated code-scanning alerts into this issue (siblings tracked separately).

## In plain English
CodeQL alert #137 flags HIGH js/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization on a unit-test assertion in github-auth-modes.provisioning.test.ts ~L174: row.includes("ghe.example.com") after --hostname. CodeQL correctly notes the host substring can appear anywhere. Prefer-A rewrites that host check to an exact argv-token / URL-host parse so alert #137 clears by a real fix without weakening the GHES --hostname provisioning intent. Suite-config / suppress as primary stays a keep-out. This is a test file only.

## Draft remedy sketch
1. In packages/core/src/intake/github-auth-modes.provisioning.test.ts, replace the flagged row.includes("--hostname") && row.includes("ghe.example.com") check with an exact host-binding assertion: locate the --hostname flag index and assert the next argv token equals "ghe.example.com" (or parse that token via URL / normalizeGithubHostname and compare host). Do not keep a substring includes of the hostname string as the clearance path.
2. Keep the existing expect(result.ok) and expect(result.githubHost).toBe("ghe.example.com") intents; do not weaken the GHES probe contract.
3. Existing unit tests for the touched module stay green; add a narrow adversarial note only if useful that a lookalike host token (for example not-ghe.example.com or ghe.example.com.evil) would not satisfy the rewritten exact-token / parsed-host check.
4. CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Security/Fixed entry citing CodeQL alert #137 / #5746.
5. Keep-out: CodeQL suite-config / path-exclude / suppress as the primary fix (issue Non-goals).

## Reject (draft)
- Treating CodeQL config / suppress / dismiss-without-fix as the primary remedy
- Bundling unrelated code-scanning alerts into this issue
- Rewriting production validateHostGhMode / resolveGithubHost beyond what the test assertion rewrite requires
- Claiming alert #137 cleared without rewriting the flagged includes site (or an evidence-backed false-positive disposition after review)

## Finding 1 — sharpen-framing
classification: sharpens-framing

Evidence: At the dispatch SHA, `githubApiArgs` emits `api --hostname <host> <path>`, `githubApiPath` already parses that argv shape, and the flagged test currently accepts any captured row containing both `--hostname` and `ghe.example.com`. Prefer-A's exact-next-token rewrite removes the CodeQL substring finding, but the draft still permits a broad `seen.some` assertion and offers URL parsing as an interchangeable option.

Failure mode: A future or malformed captured invocation could contain the expected hostname in an unrelated position, or a lookalike such as `ghe.example.com.evil` could be accepted if the implementation chooses a substring-based URL check. That would make the test green without proving the GHES hostname is the value bound to `--hostname` for the intended API probe.

Disposition consequence: Keep Prefer-A and the test-only scope, but make the acceptance criterion explicit: locate the `--hostname`/`-H` flag, require its immediate value to equal the normalized expected host, and bind the assertion to the relevant API row (using the existing `githubApiPath` helper or equivalent). Exact equality must reject lookalikes; retain `result.ok` and `result.githubHost` assertions. This is a sharpening, not a design blocker.

Road-not-taken: I do not recommend changing `resolveGithubHost` or production auth behavior; the pinned tree already has the argv construction and parsing mechanisms needed for a narrow assertion fix.
